body.x: Gbrain (Co-CEOs Byoung Kim and Seong-gu Yang) announced that it successfully secured a global export network with its cortical electrical stimulation-based brain disease patient treatment solution showcased at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition held in Las Vegas early last month.

Gbrain is a company developing new technologies to treat patients with intractable brain diseases. The company explains that it offers new possibilities with electrodes inserted directly into the cerebrum and closed-loop stimulation technology to address diseases and symptoms that existing deep brain stimulation has not sufficiently resolved.

Since its establishment in 2019, Gbrain has internalized capabilities across the entire life cycle, from research and development to manufacturing, quality, and clinical trials, focusing on fully implantable cranial nerve stimulation technology. As a result, it established infrastructure for the commercialization and supply of its products, including obtaining GMP certification for its manufacturing facility in 2024.

At the same time, Phin Stim, developed with clinical applicability and technological competitiveness, as demonstrated by winning national projects, attracted strong interest from global visitors at CES 2026. This fully implantable cranial nerve stimulator integrates ultra-thin, highly flexible cortical electrodes and circuitry, and its design adheres closely to the cortical surface to reliably acquire high-resolution brain signals.

The collected data goes beyond simple recording and is processed immediately on the device to inform treatment decisions. An AI processor integrated into the circuitry analyzes real-time brain waves to determine the patient’s neurological state and automatically adjusts stimulation parameters accordingly. It offers strong differentiation by enabling more customized treatment for patients, compared with existing stimulation methods that repeat preset stimulations.

body.cap: Introductory brochure for Phin Stim | Image provided by Gbrain

body.x: In addition, the BCI (Brain-Computer Interface) technology applied to Phin Stim enabled precise stimulation optimization and scalability across various neurological indications. Gbrain, selected for an Innovation Award for two consecutive years for its solution that combines clinical functionality and technological scalability, generated USD 57.5 million in export consulting value during the exhibition, achieving the highest performance among participating companies at the Incheon-IFEZ Pavilion.

A Gbrain official stated, “We feel pleased to promote the innovativeness of our cranial nerve stimulation system, Phin Stim, to the world by winning the Innovation Award in the Digital Health category for two consecutive years.” They added, “We gained great interest with nearly 120 consultations, and the resulting large consultation value serves as an indicator proving the global medical device market’s interest in new brain disease treatments.”

They continued, “As we confirmed both actual clinical applicability and value as a business model, we will formally pursue partnerships with global pharmaceutical companies and research institutions.” They said, “Through this, we will focus all our efforts on entering the North American market and accelerating global clinical trials to emerge as a leading company that presents practical treatment alternatives for patients with intractable brain diseases.”

body.x: Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
